records.title: TRIMS: Trajectory-Ranked Instruction Masked Supervision for Diffusion Language Models
records.reason: The primary full text confirms TRIMS is an inference-time decoding method that improves parallelism and token throughput while retaining similar accuracy; the training data curation is much cheaper than distillation but is not the basis for this classification. Body review: TRIMS is presented as low-latency DLM inference and raises parallelism/TPS up to about 3× with similar accuracy. The paper also reports 0.6 GPU-hours curation versus 287 GPU-hours distillation; this training-side comparison is separate from the inference contribution.

records.title: OTPrune: Distribution-Aligned Visual Token Pruning via Optimal Transport
records.reason: This is inference-time visual-token pruning for multimodal LLMs, reducing the vision-token burden while addressing distribution shift from pruning.

records.title: MentorCollab: Large-to-Small Inference-Time Mentorship for Concise Reasoning in Language Models
records.reason: This inference-time selective mentorship method limits large-model contribution and generated-token cost while preserving a small model as the primary generator. Full-text review found no latency measurement, so the efficiency link is token/cost reduction rather than a demonstrated speedup. Body review: The small model remains the generator and a larger mentor is used selectively; the paper reports an 18.4% average mentor-token share in final responses. The reviewed text did not provide an end-to-end latency measurement, so a speedup is not established.

records.title: HeRo-Q: A General Framework for Stable Low Bit Quantization via Hessian Conditioning
records.reason: This enables low-bit LLM inference with reduced model memory and little extra runtime computation.

records.title: Towards Understanding Best Practices for Quantization of Vision-Language Models
records.reason: It studies low-bit deployment of vision-language models, with inference memory and latency as the optimization targets.

records.title: Ken: An Execution Engine for Unstructured Database Systems
records.reason: The engine schedules model invocations and places operators across GPUs to optimize query latency/accuracy trade-offs; this is an inference execution and scheduling contribution. The primary paper abstract reports the stated latency comparisons. Body review: The official PVLDB paper describes dynamic cascades for database ML inference, GPU placement, and invocation scheduling. Its abstract reports 1.7–3.3× and up to 122× latency reductions against the stated baselines; only abstract, introduction, background, and system description were reviewed.

records.title: Streaming Tensor Programs: A Streaming Abstraction for Dynamic Parallelism
records.reason: The streaming abstraction targets runtime scheduling and utilization for dynamic tensor/LLM workloads, with reported latency and utilization improvements.

records.title: EPARA: Parallelizing Categorized AI Inference in Edge Clouds
records.reason: It is an edge-cloud inference resource-allocation method with an explicit serving goodput result.

records.title: EE-Tuning: An Economical yet Scalable Solution for Tuning Early-Exit Large Language Models
records.reason: Early exit reduces inference computation for LLMs; the paper is an inference-efficiency method even though it requires tuning/training to prepare the exits.

records.title: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
